data.title: Security-Tool Tampering and Indicator Blocking
data.summary: The sample disables, uninstalls, or tampers with the configuration of installed security tools before or during its main activity, rather than attempting to evade them covertly.
data.description:
This is a direct rather than stealthy move: terminating the endpoint agent's process,
uninstalling it via its own management interface, unloading its kernel driver, or editing
its configuration to exclude the sample's own paths. It requires elevated privilege and is
correspondingly a strong signal once observed — legitimate software essentially never
disables a different vendor's security product.
data.recommendation:
* Alert on termination, service-stop, or driver-unload events targeting any installed security product, treating it as high-confidence malicious regardless of the actor.
* Protect the security product's own process and configuration with tamper protection where the vendor offers it.
* Where tampering succeeded, assume detection coverage was blind for the affected window and widen the investigation accordingly.
data.short_recommendation: Alert on any process, service or driver action targeting an installed security product as high-confidence malicious.

mitre_techniques.procedure: Called the endpoint agent's own management API to add an exclusion covering its own payload directory.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Issued the security product's uninstall command via its management interface rather than attempting covert evasion.
